page: Amazon Web Services m8id.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture utilizing a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 4 vCPUs, 2 physical cores, and 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. System memory consists of 16.0 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2052.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 34.06 GB/sec. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling present a performance tradeoff. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is categorized as weak at 4318.27, and the multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 28.9 GB/sec is similarly limited. Large block memory bandwidth is average, reaching 44.5 GB/sec for read operations and 31.41 GB/sec for write operations. For specialized workloads, the processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for matrix operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8id.xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads requiring high single-thread performance and fast local temporary storage. The inclusion of the 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store provides high-speed local I/O without the added cost of external block storage, though data on this volume is ephemeral. This server is suitable for single-threaded applications, text processing, lightweight web serving, and software compilation. It is less optimal for highly parallelized multi-threaded tasks, database operations, or medium-to-large language model inference due to its lower multi-core scaling and memory capacity.
